summary: The operator-recovery experiment executed (receipt 0440f054115e44f4a0234c7a4ef67150) and both comparisons scored as predicted: the state reproduced first (zero servers, no leader in two seconds, staged commit 6, log last index 7), live bootstrap on the running node failed with 'bootstrap only works on new clusters' and left the configuration empty (violated, index 1 — the documented refusal, since BootstrapCluster checks existing state and returns ErrCantBootstrap), while RecoverCluster on the stopped node succeeded and the next NewRaft came up with one server and led within three seconds (holds, index 2), because it snapshots the supplied configuration and truncates the log so the next start restores from the snapshot instead of the skipped prefix. The third child investigation is now recorded with conclusion explained and no defect claim — neither behaviour is a defect, and the point is operational: the library offers a repair path for a stopped node but not for a running one. The parent interpretation replaces its pending note with the executed result and states the complete repair picture: a later configuration entry from a correctly configured leader, a restart with the flag disabled, or RecoverCluster on a stopped node work; live bootstrap and an incoming snapshot for a complete-log node do not.
